**Group:** Diatoms  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

Cells are circular in valve view and disc- to drum-shaped, with areolae in radial or fasciculate rows and a ring of marginal processes. They frequently form loose chains held together by a single thin organic thread extruded from a central process, or occur singly. Key features: circular valve, radial areolae, central-thread linkage rather than marginal tubes.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **skeletonema** | Skeletonema is bridged by a ring of long marginal tubes leaving a clear gap; Thalassiosira chains hang from one fine central thread with cells close together. |
| **centric** | Use Thalassiosira when the disc shape and central-thread chains are evident; use Centric when the genus can't be resolved. |
